feedback: Written before this candidate races. Evidence from earlier iterations: the ±0.03 m row at 16 mm with kp 1.2 and kd 0.4 is the best raced design, at 69.46 in iterations 3, 5, 6, 7 and 9, so the simulator is deterministic for this layout (iteration 3). Max error sits near 0.062 m on every track, so the off-track limit is still the binding failure (iterations 3 to 9). Iteration 3 showed s-bend oscillation rising to 0.168, so your edge-noise hypothesis is reasonable. The 12 mm test at ±0.02 m (iteration 2, 63.85) was a different row and cannot isolate this. Iteration 8 showed that ±0.04 m at kp 1.2 scores 61.35 (iteration 8, which matches iteration 4 per track), so the wider row is worse on its own. I have held the controller at kp 1.2, kd 0.4 and base_speed 1.1. I did not change gains for the smaller footprint in this race, so the footprint effect can be read directly. Do not expect a new best from this candidate. Your reach estimate of about 0.0485 m is consistent with the iteration 2 and 3 coverage evidence. When this race reports, read s-bend oscillation against 0.168 and s-bend progress against 0.210, and count line-loss events against the 1.0 to 1.1 per run seen at 16 mm.
requested_changes: If the score falls below 69.46 or line loss rises above 1.1 per run, return to the 16 mm footprint at x = ±0.03 m, y = 0.04 (iteration 3 layout), since the 12 mm reach of about 0.0485 m is then the limit.

If s-bend steering oscillation falls below 0.168 with s-bend progress held near 0.21, keep 12 mm at ±0.03 m as the candidate for the final design, and hold the Integrator's kp 1.2 and kd 0.4 without changes.

If the next race shows a stronger response to edge changes (steering oscillation rising on the slalom above 0.15), do not move the row forward on this evidence alone. Hold the footprint and report the slalom oscillation, since the forward offset trigger has not been met at any row tested.
